contexts.text: Among these, open-sourced frameworks like OpenHands (Wang et al., 2024b) have gained popularity due to their strong user experience. More- over, scientific discovery (Jansen et al., 2024; Lu et al., 2024a) and ML agents (Yang et al., 2024b) are also receiving increased attention.   LLM-as-a-Judge In the domain of AI evaluation and judgment, frameworks (Zheng et al., 2024; Fu et al., 2024; Chen et al.) have pioneered the use of LLMs to assess conversational agents, demon- strating how LLMs can evaluate dialogue quality and consistency. Expanding beyond dialogue, LLMs like CodeR (Chen et al., 2024a) and MASAI (Arora et al., 2024) apply similar judging prin- ciples to the code validation process, where AI systems autonomously evaluate and verify computer programs. Our work builds on these advancements by exploring how LLMs can perform more nuanced judgment tasks, further investigating their potential in decision-making across various do- mains.

contexts.text: To check whether the LLM-judged quality scores are trustworthy, we compare them with scores from two human experts on 50 proposals generated by 9 systems. The two annotators scored the same quality dimensions as the LLM judges. Figure 4(a) reports two Pearson correlations: between the two annotators on individual proposals, and between each LLM judge and the averaged human scores. We make two observations. First, scoring research proposals is inherently subjective, and even the two experts disagree to a notable degree (r = 0.56), much as reviewers do in conference peer review. Second, each LLM judge correlates with the human average at a level comparable to the agreement between the two annotators (r = 0.51–0.59 for top-3 judges). LLM judges are therefore a reasonable proxy for expert assessment.   Figure 4(b–c) further measures two properties of each judge: its agreement with the cross-judge consensus, and its self-preference bias toward generation systems from its own model family. Qwen3.6-27B agrees strongly with the consensus, second only to the frontier Claude-4.8 judge, and the difference between the two is not statistically significant. Its self-preference bias is negligible and lower than Claude-4.8’s, justifying why we chose it as the main judge.
